title: 6 Oct 2026 (Hail)
des: Saudi Prometric paediatrics recall, Hail, 6 October 2026

questions.question: A child suddenly cannot stand after a URTI; he is otherwise normal except for ataxia and CT is normal. What is the diagnosis?
A 10-month-old has brief episodes of head and arm extension, and EEG shows spikes and waves. What is the diagnosis?
A child with meningitis on ceftriaxone has a negative rapid Haemophilus test. What should be done?
An infant has fever, rash, bulging fontanelle, HR 160 and BP 60/40. What is the first treatment after antibiotics?
questions.exp: Treat shock first even with meningitis.

questions.question: An infant falls head-first down stairs, is fully conscious, then becomes drowsy an hour later. What is the diagnosis?
A child has a right optic nerve astrocytoma. Which disease is associated?
A child with otitis media on amoxicillin for 5 days becomes irritable. What is the investigation?
A child has recurrent abdominal pain with headache. What is the diagnosis?
A child has leg hypotonia, reduced reflexes and a positive Babinski sign. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Acute cord lesion in spinal shock. The recall writer recorded tuberous sclerosis, which does not fit.

questions.question: A child with diarrhoea and dehydration develops a flank mass and haematuria. What is the diagnosis?
What is the best investigation for renal vein thrombosis?
A child has hypertension, red cells and some pus cells in urine. What is the diagnosis?
A child on treatment for constipation has fever, pyuria and haematuria. What test assesses renal involvement?
questions.exp: DMSA in acute pyelonephritis. Culture comes first.

questions.question: How is beta-thalassaemia trait diagnosed?
A child has thrombocytopenia with small platelets. What is the diagnosis?
Why do children with sickle cell disease get recurrent pneumonia?
questions.c: Functional asplenia with low properdin (alternative complement pathway)

questions.question: A haemophilia patient does not improve after factor VIII. What is next?
A child with tetralogy of Fallot has a hypercyanotic spell with tachycardia and tachypnoea. Central pulses are good. Which drug relaxes the infundibulum?
questions.exp: Beta-blockers reduce infundibular spasm after oxygen, knee-chest and morphine.

questions.question: A child with cyanotic heart disease has vomiting and right-sided weakness. What is the diagnosis?
A child has an ejection systolic murmur and wide fixed splitting of S2. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Flow murmur across the pulmonary valve.

questions.question: A child with heart failure is on digoxin and furosemide. What is added next?
A child is unresponsive and pulseless with VF on the monitor. What is the treatment?
A child has severe right lower abdominal pain, vomiting and diarrhoea and looks unwell. What is the first step?
questions.c: IV fluids and IV antibiotics with surgical review

questions.question: What is the best investigation for hypertrophic pyloric stenosis?
questions.exp: Pylorus thickness ≥ 3-4 mm and length ≥ 15 mm.

questions.question: What is the initial management of congenital diaphragmatic hernia at birth?
questions.exp: Decompress the stomach; surgery after stabilisation.
questions.a: Intubate (avoid bag-mask) and insert a large-bore NG tube

questions.question: A newborn passed little meconium, has persistent vomiting and multiple dilated loops. What is the management?
questions.c: Resuscitate with IV fluids and refer for laparotomy

questions.question: A child has yellowish sclerae but normal labs and normal bilirubin. What is next?
questions.exp: Normal bilirubin excludes jaundice; carotenaemia spares the sclerae, so the recall is ambiguous. The recall writer chose ultrasound.
questions.c: Check diet for carotenaemia and reassure

questions.question: In which condition may probiotics be used?
questions.exp: Probiotics have evidence in antibiotic-associated diarrhoea and NEC prevention. The recall writer chose cystic fibrosis.

questions.question: A baby has vomiting, distension and multiple air-fluid levels. What is the action?
A 2-month-old breastfed baby cries more than 3 hours a day and examination is normal. What is the diagnosis?
A 10-year-old who eats junk food and watches TV 5 hours a day has soiling with a normal examination. What is the management?
A 5-year-old with ADHD is struggling at school. What is the first approach?
A 4-year-old repeats sounds and words. What is the management?
questions.exp: The recall writer chose speech therapy referral.
questions.c: Refer to speech therapy if persistent or distressing

questions.question: A 12-year-old boy has unilateral breast enlargement and pubic hair. What is the management?
What is the energy requirement of a 4-year-old?
questions.exp: Holliday-Segar: 1400 kcal for a 16-kg child, roughly 90 kcal/kg.

questions.question: A term newborn has cyanosis and apnoea worse when feeding and better when crying. What is the quickest diagnostic step?
questions.a: Pass a catheter through each nostril

questions.question: A child throws a ball and runs to fetch it, and can scribble a line. What is the age?
questions.exp: Throws ball and scribbles at 15-18 months; imitates a vertical line at 2 years. The recall writer was unsure.

questions.question: A 3-month-old has mild fever and runny nose, then worsening cough after 2 days. What is the most likely cause?
An 8-year-old with sickle cell disease is tired and pale, with Hb 3.1 g/dL. Which virus causes this?
A newborn has a red rash in the neck folds with satellite lesions. What is the treatment?
A healthy 18-month-old has unilateral nasal obstruction with foul discharge. What is the diagnosis?
A child snores at night. What is the investigation?
A child with recurrent pneumonias has low IgA and IgG and ataxia. What is the diagnosis?
A 13-year-old has raised bilirubin and Wilson disease is suspected. Which test helps?
questions.exp: Low ceruloplasmin, high urinary copper, KF rings.

questions.question: A child with seizures has a facial port-wine stain since birth. What finding supports the diagnosis?
A boy has features of fragile X. How is it diagnosed?
A 15-year-old girl has short stature, webbed neck and no breast development. What is next?
In which group is MMR vaccine still given when not severely immunosuppressed?
questions.exp: MMR is given in HIV if CD4 ≥ 15%.

questions.question: A 4-year-old had febrile seizures in the last 6 months. What about his vaccines?
questions.exp: Febrile seizures do not contraindicate vaccination.

questions.question: A child with leukaemia has household contacts. Which vaccine should contacts not receive?
What is the empirical treatment of acute osteomyelitis in a child?
questions.exp: Staph aureus. The recall writer chose vancomycin.
questions.b: Anti-staphylococcal antibiotic (cefazolin or clindamycin; vancomycin if MRSA common)

questions.question: How is SMA type 1 with tongue fasciculation diagnosed?
How does breast milk differ from formula?
questions.exp: Breast milk is whey-dominant with lower protein. The recall writer said breast milk has more protein, which is incorrect.
questions.c: Breast milk has less protein but more easily digested whey and protective factors

questions.question: A 4-year-old boy is 125 cm; father 178 cm, mother 157 cm. What is his target height?
What is the first step in suspected acute UTI?
A child with gastroenteritis and dehydration has head lag, but development was normal. What should be done?
A child swallowed a foreign body seen on X-ray. What is the management?
questions.exp: Batteries in the oesophagus need emergency removal. The recall writer chose fluoroscopy with magnet.
questions.a: Depends on site and type; oesophageal coins need endoscopic removal

questions.question: A 2-month-old has become very pale with Hb 6, normal WBC and platelets and normal indices. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: TEC occurs after 1 year; physiological anaemia does not drop to 6.

questions.question: A child has ascending weakness. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bladder involvement is unusual and suggests a cord lesion.

questions.question: For contact precautions, what is done first?
What is the daily maintenance fluid for a 20-kg child?
questions.exp: Holliday-Segar: 1000 + 50 × 10 = 1500 mL/day. The recall writer recorded 1000.

questions.question: A 10-year-old girl has renal features after pharyngitis, with normal BP and platelets. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Usually 1-3 weeks after pharyngitis; synpharyngitic haematuria suggests IgA.

questions.question: What is the length gain per month in months 3-6?
An immunocompromised child with a central line develops infection after 10 days in hospital. What is the empirical treatment?
A child on prednisolone 2 mg/kg/day for more than 14 days is due live vaccines. What should be done?
questions.exp: High-dose steroids (≥ 2 mg/kg or ≥ 20 mg/day for ≥ 14 days) delay live vaccines for 1 month.
questions.b: Defer live vaccines until 1 month after stopping

questions.question: A child refuses his father's orders and kicks things. What is the diagnosis?
A 10-year-old has gastric volvulus and an NG tube cannot be passed. What is the treatment?
An exclusively breastfed newborn who did not receive vitamin K bleeds with prolonged PT and PTT. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Breast milk is low in vitamin K.
questions.b: Haemorrhagic disease of the newborn (vitamin K deficiency bleeding)

questions.question: A newborn has microcephaly, rash and hepatosplenomegaly; the mother had a flu-like illness in pregnancy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Blueberry muffin rash. CMV is also possible.

questions.question: Which condition causes a false negative Mantoux test?
Which condition causes a false negative sweat chloride test?
What does the Swiss cheese model describe?
questions.c: How multiple system defences fail together, allowing an error

questions.question: A short infant has a high-pitched cry and micropenis. What should be measured?
In which condition can Bartter-like features occur?
What is a consequence of repeated unnecessary antibiotics?
What is the main role of a CPR team leader?
questions.b: Coordinate the team with clear communication

questions.question: A child was sexually abused by a teacher. What should be done?
questions.d: Report to the police and child protection services

questions.question: A drug company offers money to sponsor a doctor's conference trip. What is the ethical action?
What does mortality rate mean?
questions.exp: Case fatality is deaths among cases.
questions.a: The number of deaths in a population over a period

questions.question: An infant has coarse facies, large tongue, umbilical hernia and lethargy. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: The recall picture had no clear details.

questions.question: A child has meningitis with Gram-negative diplococci. What is the organism and treatment?
An older child has green vomiting and a corkscrew duodenum. What is the diagnosis?
A newborn has pustules that leave pigmented macules. What is the diagnosis?
A newborn has an occipital skin-covered sac with brain tissue. What is the diagnosis?
A child has painful swelling behind the ear pushing the ear forward after otitis media. How is mastoiditis confirmed?
questions.exp: CT shows coalescence or abscess; culture fluid at surgery.
questions.d: Contrast CT of the temporal bone

questions.question: A toxic child drools and has stridor. What is the diagnosis?
A child has sudden breathlessness with absent breath sounds on one side and a black hemithorax on X-ray. What is the diagnosis?
A child has crops of itchy vesicles at different stages. What is the diagnosis?
A mother leaves a meeting and refuses to hear about her child's illness; the father stays. What should the doctor do?
questions.exp: Either parent can receive information and consent.

questions.question: A child with a cochlear implant was injured in a road accident, the ER doctor missed it and he was later found to have hearing loss. What type of error is it?
questions.b: Diagnostic error requiring a systems approach

questions.question: A new resident is waiting for the consultant when another senior arrives. What should happen?
questions.c: Give a structured handover to the senior

questions.question: Parents refuse life-saving dialysis for their child. What should be done?
questions.d: Give dialysis in the child's best interest

questions.question: A colleague is neglecting a patient. What should you do first?
